acceptance_rows.result: Protocol 1 bindings start with captured configuration. Injected transport fixtures execute through that binding.
Every frozen event support claim has a positive or unsupported fixture. Zero/one/many deliveries retain order and stable provider item identity.
Every frozen operation support claim has a native, fallback or unsupported result fixture. Assertions check exact provider calls, cached request results, native serialization and trace.
Declared queries retain items and cursors. Streams remain lazy. Resource ownership, cancellation, expiry and failure are checked. Provider controls stay private.

Complete limits reject before the sink. Error, raise, throw, exit and invalid sink results have explicit call/effect assertions. Acceptance, acknowledgement and retry behavior match the frozen transport rule.

transport_contract.delivery_identity: binding ID plus upsert batch ID, or ordered message IDs with bounded canonical digest
transport_contract.item_identity: batch identity plus message ID and ordinal
transport_contract.acceptance: Normalize and accept a complete upsert unit; retain order and report sink rejection. Connection/pairing/QR/private controls stay outside public Signal data.
transport_contract.acknowledgement: Amarula acquisition can occur before sink acceptance. No provider checkpoint or durable replay guarantee is added.
transport_contract.retry_unit: upsert batch; preserve existing connection management, report rejection, and make no invented provider retry claim

acceptance_rows.result: One complete Amarula upsert produces one sink call. SDK edit/revoke tuples retain their targets. Cold reaction clear preserves an unknown emoji as null. QR, pairing and profile controls remain private. Sink failures have no accepted effects.

proof_reuse: Package source, tests and configuration match the successful end snapshots. Formatting precedes quality checks. Older positive tests for Signal, Mattermost and Teams remain valid: the only later core library change allows null for a required ReactionRemoved value. Current G6 fixtures, shared catalog checks and schema tests verify that correction. Telegram/Slack code is unchanged from B3 and their package and runtime fixtures were refreshed.
